summary:
Orbital Frontier is a web-based Space Mission Design Game built by Team ZYRANOVA to make space engineering simple, interactive, and fun for students. Players become Chief Mission Architect: they pick a mission, build a spacecraft in an interactive 3D view, choose a rocket, fix every system warning, and launch. Along the way they must handle emergency events and manage tight budgets, with difficulty levels from Cadet to Commander. Scores and five achievements reward smart engineering decisions.
The game answers the challenge of teaching space mission design by turning complex ideas such as budget, power, mass, and rocket selection into hands-on choices with instant feedback. It uses simulated educational data, not real NASA telemetry, so it stays safe and accessible.
It matters because students learn by doing. They practise problem-solving, planning, and decision-making under pressure, which builds STEM curiosity and prepares the next generation of explorers.
details:
​Orbital Frontier is an interactive web-based platform designed to explore and visualize space missions, telemetry data, and satellite tracking in real time through an intuitive, user-friendly interface.

It streamlines complex orbital data into clear, accessible visual modules, making space metrics easily understandable for researchers, students, and space enthusiasts alike.

The project aims to democratize space data accessibility, inspire STEM engagement, and provide a scalable tool for educational and observational use worldwide.

Built using modern web technologies—including HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, and Vercel for cloud hosting—the platform balances fast client-side rendering with low-latency updates.

Creatively, our team prioritized a modular component architecture and high-contrast space-themed UI/UX layout, carefully balancing deep technical accuracy with rapid, responsive performance under tight hackathon constraints.
